extracted.intended_audience: theater critics, arts journalists, editors, and students of theatre criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for which theatrical productions are considered newsworthy to review (especially around opening night) and the specific evaluative criteria critics use when assessing productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews not published until after official opening night
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are typically not published until after a production's official opening night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics may attend preview performances once the production is 'frozen' but reviews are embargoed and generally drop on or after opening day. Historically critics often attended the opening night itself, but modern practice has shifted toward preview viewing and embargoed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics attend preview performances after show 'frozen'
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics typically attend preview performances after the production has reached a 'frozen' state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview attendance allows critics to see the show prior to opening while expecting minimal further creative changes; such coverage is embargoed until the official opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed until opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Critic reviews are commonly embargoed and held until the production's official opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargo practice governs timing of publication so that reviews coincide with the opening rather than earlier previews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Broadway productions
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale Broadway shows are primary subjects for formal reviews due to their scale and visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadway productions generally merit coverage by major outlets because of their industry impact, budgets, and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-Broadway / Off-Off Broadway with buzz
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller New York productions are reviewed when they generate significant buzz or attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all Off/Off-Off Broadway work is covered; selection depends on perceived interest, novelty, or critical attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional theater in major markets (LA, Chicago)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noteworthy regional productions in major theater cities are candidates for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional work in influential markets may be covered because it contributes to the national theater conversation and is accessible to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival productions (Edinburgh, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows presented at prominent festivals are considered newsworthy for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival contexts concentrate new and experimental work and attract press attention, making these productions reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star vehicles (major celebrity attached)
rubrics_metrics.description: Productions featuring major celebrity performers are often reviewed due to public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Star attachment increases newsworthiness regardless of production scale, drawing readers and influencing coverage decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Famous director projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Productions directed by well-known or influential directors are likely to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director reputation can make a production newsworthy for analysis of vision and staging choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: New work by established playwright
rubrics_metrics.description: Premieres of new plays by recognized playwrights are considered newsworthy review subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new play from an established writer attracts attention for its contribution to the artist's oeuvre and contemporary discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revivals of classics
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-stagings of canonical works are reviewed, particularly when noteworthy or distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical interest centers on interpretation, production choices, and relevance of the classic to contemporary audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative / experimental work
rubrics_metrics.description: Avant-garde or formally innovative productions are considered for coverage based on creativity and boundary-pushing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such work merits review when it contributes new forms, techniques, or dialogues to theater practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revivals at major regional theaters
rubrics_metrics.description: Revivals staged at significant regional institutions are reviewworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major regional houses can mount revivals with artistic or cultural weight deserving critical attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touring productions in their stop city
rubrics_metrics.description: Touring shows are reviewed when they make a local stop and are accessible to local audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Touring productions bring high-profile work to different cities and often attract local review coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: High school / community theater in local press
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller-scale community and school productions may be reviewed by local outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local news coverage can treat community theater as culturally significant within its community even if not of national interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction (vision, pace, integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the director's overarching vision, pacing, and integration of production elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics evaluate how effectively direction shapes performance, coherence, and storytelling; look for clarity of concept, rhythm, and unity among design and performance elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting performances (lead and ensemble)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of lead and ensemble acting quality and appropriateness for the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique includes characterization, emotional truth, chemistry, consistency, and whether performances serve the production's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set design
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and appropriateness of scenic design and its contribution to storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider functionality, aesthetics, symbolism, and how set supports mood and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lighting design
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of lighting in creating atmosphere, focus, and visual clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments consider mood, transitions, visibility, and how lighting interacts with other design elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound design
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and impact of sound, including effects, amplification, and sonic environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, balance, design creativity, and contribution to narrative and emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costume design
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness and artistry of costumes for character, period, and production concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how costumes inform character, movement, and visual cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choreography (musicals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of choreography within musical productions for inventiveness and integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at movement vocabulary, clarity, energy, and how dance furthers story and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music direction (musicals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of musical leadership, orchestration, and vocal/instrumental performance in musicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate musical balance, interpretation, singers' support, and overall musical cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playwright's craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the playwright's writing skills and structural command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics consider character development, scene construction, dramatic tension, and craft details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themes addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance and treatment of themes within the play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether themes are handled with depth, nuance, and relevance to contemporary concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the play's spoken text for authenticity, wit, and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clarity of voice, subtext, and whether dialogue advances character and plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure / pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: How the play's structure and pacing affect dramatic momentum and audience engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique considers scene distribution, rhythm, and whether the work maintains narrative propulsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs. derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment of whether the work feels original or merely derivative of other works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics note novelty of ideas, approaches, and the work's contribution versus its reliance on tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a play or production speaks to current cultural dialogues or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate topicality, resonance, and whether the work meaningfully engages with cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the production moves or affects the audience emotionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics report on emotional clarity, authenticity, and whether intended emotional beats land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the production stimulates thought, raises questions, or provokes reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess complexity, thematic depth, ambiguity, and opportunities for critical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: How memorable the production is—how long it lingers with the viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider standout moments, originality, and lasting impressions beyond the performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation worthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the critic would recommend the production to potential audience members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation often synthesizes quality, audience fit, and overall value judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket-price value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the production is worth its ticket price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics may consider production scale, quality, and audience expectations in judging value for money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening night parties (entertainment news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social events associated with openings that are newsworthy outside of formal reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening night parties are often covered in entertainment pages for celebrity presence, fashion, and social signaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star casting announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: News coverage of high-profile casting decisions independent of performance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements generate pre-opening interest and can be treated as news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production drama (firings, walkouts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Behind-the-scenes controversies such as firings or cast walkouts that become news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such events are covered as news because they affect the production's trajectory and industry perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports on ticket-sales achievements or notable commercial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong box-office figures can be newsworthy indicators of public interest and financial success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tony nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards recognition (e.g., Tony nominations) which generate news and retrospective coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award nominations and wins elevate a production's profile and merit both news pieces and critical reassessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: News that a production will close, particularly unexpectedly or early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures can be covered for their business implications and impact on audiences and talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production scale (Broadway > regional > community)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion that larger-scale productions are typically more newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale affects coverage priority: Broadway productions often outrank regional and community work in national coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attached talent (star, director, playwright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit emphasis on the presence of well-known artists as a driver of newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile attachments increase likelihood of review and broader public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural significance (major work, anniversary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Productions tied to significant cultural moments, milestones, or anniversaries are more newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance can derive from historical importance, social resonance, or institutional milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in form or content
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit value placed on formal or substantive innovation as a reason to cover a production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative work can signal shifts in the field and attract critical attention for experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local presence (audience can attend)
rubrics_metrics.description: A production's physical accessibility to a publication's audience increases its newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local relevance matters: outlets prioritize coverage of work audiences can actually see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited engagement (urgency for review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-run or limited engagements create urgency and therefore newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited availability can prompt timely reviews to inform audiences before the run ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential or realized commercial effects that make a production newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial performance can influence coverage decisions as it signals audience demand and industry impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood of awards recognition increases a production's newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and outlets may prioritize work that appears likely to be nominated for major awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry trend representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Productions that exemplify or signal larger trends in theater are considered newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage can focus on how a production fits into broader movements or changes in the field.
